summary:
We developed Luna, an interactive lunar exploration platform designed to help users explore, analyze, and evaluate potential landing sites on the Moon. Built around NASA-sourced lunar datasets, LUNA transforms complex scientific information into an intuitive and accessible environment for lunar mission planning.

Users can navigate the lunar surface, explore landing locations using geographic coordinates, examine terrain characteristics, and compare multiple potential landing sites based on relevant scientific and operational factors. The platform also incorporates mission-oriented information, including surface elevation, terrain slope, roughness, crater density, sunlight conditions, and communication considerations.

LUNA addresses the challenge of making lunar landing-site assessment more accessible, understandable, and efficient by bringing diverse datasets together in one interactive platform. Beyond supporting researchers and mission planners, it aims to inspire students, educators, and the next generation of space explorers by making lunar exploration an engaging, hands-on experience.
details:
LUNA is an interactive lunar exploration and landing-site assessment platform developed to make scientific lunar data accessible, understandable, and useful for mission planning. Instead of presenting users with disconnected datasets, LUNA brings multiple sources of lunar information into a unified, interactive environment where the Moon itself becomes the primary interface.

Users can explore the lunar surface through an interactive 3D environment, navigate locations using latitude and longitude, search for geographical features or mission locations, and investigate potential landing sites. The platform also provides a specialized 2D topographic view of the lunar South Pole, allowing users to examine the region in greater detail.

LUNA integrates NASA-sourced lunar datasets to provide meaningful information about potential landing locations. Users can examine several important factors, including surface elevation, terrain slope, surface roughness, crater density, terrain classification, sunlight conditions, and communication considerations such as Direct-to-Earth (DTE) availability.

The platform supports landing-site comparison, enabling users to evaluate multiple locations side by side. Users can select predefined locations or explore custom coordinates, compare relevant scientific factors, and generate a structured comparison dossier. Mission-duration considerations further help users understand how different landing locations may affect operational planning.

LUNA is designed to distinguish between available scientific information and unavailable data. Where reliable information is not available, the platform indicates that the data is unavailable rather than presenting fabricated values.

The platform was developed primarily using React and Vite, with JavaScript, HTML, and CSS for its interactive frontend and user interface. We incorporated geospatial visualization, interactive mapping, 3D rendering, and data-processing techniques to transform scientific datasets into an accessible exploration experience.

Our development process involved researching and integrating publicly available scientific datasets, understanding their formats and geographical references, and considering how different datasets could contribute to landing-site evaluation.

We also used AI-assisted development tools, including Google AI Studio, ChatGPT, Claude, and Antigravity. These tools supported interface development, code generation, debugging, technical research, feasibility evaluation, and prompt refinement. Dataset selection, scientific considerations, feature decisions, integration, and final implementation were part of our team's development process.

Our central design decision was to make the Moon the interface rather than treating it as another background visualization. We wanted users to discover scientific information through exploration instead of navigating complicated technical dashboards.

LUNA is intended not only for researchers and mission planners but also for students, educators, and people interested in space exploration. By connecting scientific data with an intuitive visual experience, we aim to lower the barrier to understanding lunar geography and mission planning.

Our long-term vision is to expand LUNA into a more comprehensive lunar mission-planning environment, incorporating additional validated datasets, improved environmental analysis, more mission scenarios, and advanced landing-site assessment capabilities. Ultimately, we hope to make the process of understanding and planning future lunar exploration more accessible to everyone.
